periods.analysis: Primary care access is green at 87.6%, above the 85% target and a strong starting point for this run. The summer panel review showed the best gains among adults with diabetes and children due for well visits after Harborview Health and Seabreeze Family Medicine added Saturday preventive-care blocks. This matters because timely primary care is where we find hypertension, depression, and vaccine gaps before they become emergency visits.
periods.recommendations: Sustain the Saturday preventive-care blocks through October and reserve at least 20% of those slots for patients overdue for annual visits. Extend the South Harbor text-recall cohort to Spanish and Vietnamese messages so the access gain is shared across neighborhoods, not just among patients already comfortable using the portal.

periods.analysis: Access remains green at 86.8%, down 0.8 points from 87.6% but still above target. The decline is consistent with holiday provider leave, respiratory-season demand, and two short weeks at the Harborview Community Clinic. Staff protected preventive access by keeping nurse-triage scripts focused on same-week primary care rather than default urgent-care referral.
periods.recommendations: Keep the respiratory-season triage protocol in place through February and audit 50 redirected calls per month for appropriateness and equity. For the next holiday period, publish provider leave coverage six weeks earlier and pre-open chronic-disease follow-up slots for high-risk panels.

periods.analysis: Access improved to 87.3%, up 0.5 points from 86.8%, keeping Harborview in green territory. The winter recovery came from the Cedar Point appointment-release pilot, where unused specialty holds were converted to primary care visits every Thursday afternoon. That is a practical prevention win because it moved patients with asthma, hypertension, and medication-refill needs into routine care before avoidable exacerbations.
periods.recommendations: Make the Thursday hold-conversion pilot permanent at Cedar Point and add a simple dashboard showing slots released, filled, and unused. Extend the same workflow to Bayside Pediatrics for well-child visits before summer camp and school-form demand arrives.

periods.analysis: Access rose to 89%, up 1.7 points from 87.3%, the strongest quarter so far in this sequence. The gain tracks with the May launch of the Harborview Access Line, the Route 6 clinic shuttle partnership, and outreach to Medicaid renewal cohorts before coverage lapses translated into missed care. The result is green and clinically meaningful because earlier access supports immunizations, cancer screening, and medication continuity.
periods.recommendations: Sustain the Access Line staffing model with bilingual coverage during the 7:00-9:00 a.m. call surge and report abandonment rates by ZIP code. Extend the Route 6 shuttle vouchers to prenatal and post-discharge primary care visits, where missed appointments carry higher clinical risk.

periods.analysis: Access is 88%, down 1 point from 89% but still green and comfortably above the 85% target. The dip is not surprising given summer population pressure, two nurse practitioner vacancies, and back-to-school physical demand concentrated at the North Pier and Marina clinics. Even with that pressure, the system held because standing orders kept vaccines and basic screenings moving without unnecessary physician bottlenecks.
periods.recommendations: Fill the two nurse practitioner vacancies with temporary coverage for September and October while permanent recruitment continues. Sustain standing-order workflows for vaccines and screenings, and add four evening back-to-school clinics next August to flatten the seasonal spike.

periods.analysis: Access edged up to 88.3%, up 0.3 points from 88%, maintaining green performance after the summer squeeze. The flu-shot plus primary-care co-scheduling campaign helped convert vaccine visits into blood-pressure checks, A1c orders, and overdue annual exams. That is the right population-health pattern: use every contact to prevent the next preventable visit.
periods.recommendations: Continue co-scheduling flu vaccination with primary-care gap closure and add mammography and colorectal-screening prompts to the rooming checklist. Review no-show patterns from the Marina clinic by insurance type and offer targeted reminder calls for patients with two or more missed visits.

periods.analysis: Access reached 90.1%, up 1.8 points from 88.3%, the best result in this eight-quarter arc. The improvement followed the January eConsult triage expansion, which shifted low-complexity dermatology and endocrinology questions back to primary care management without making patients wait for specialty appointments. Harborview is using its healthy operating position well here: practical infrastructure is improving prevention, not just adding volume.
periods.recommendations: Sustain eConsult triage and measure whether resolved cases receive follow-up within 30 days, especially for diabetes and hypertension. Extend the model to behavioral health medication questions with clear protocols so primary care teams can act safely and quickly.

periods.analysis: Access is 89.2%, down 0.9 points from 90.1% but still green and above target. The decrease reflects spring in-migration, tourist-season staffing competition, and new-patient demand in the East Harbor growth corridor, not a loss of basic system control. The important point is that Harborview stayed near 90% while absorbing a larger panel and onboarding two new family physicians at Clinic Site HV-PC-04.
periods.recommendations: Keep the HV-PC-04 onboarding plan on schedule and protect new-patient slots from being consumed by routine refill visits. Extend the high-performing Access Line and shuttle supports into East Harbor, then review June-to-August appointment lag weekly so the city can respond before access slips further.

periods.analysis: The 89.2% figure is June history carried into September, not a fresh access reading. Although it exceeds the 85% target, the previous quarter's decline and new-patient demand in East Harbor warrant caution until appointment data are checked.
periods.recommendations: Review Access Line and HV-PC-04 appointment records for September, including new-patient waits, before confirming the quarter's access status. Protect new-patient slots if waits are lengthening.
